problem: PDO is described as if it alone connects to MySQL. PDO is a uniform access layer; it needs a driver (pdo_mysql) before it can reach MySQL, so a student may think installing PDO is enough.
fix: PHP connects to MySQL through the mysqli extension, or through PDO with the pdo_mysql driver loaded.

problem: "Tomcat unpacks it on start" is only the copy-before-start case. With the default autoDeploy setting, a WAR copied while Tomcat is running is also deployed and exploded without a restart, so the sentence can mislead a student debugging a live server.
fix: Copy shop.war into webapps. Tomcat deploys it as the context /shop and unpacks it into a folder of the same name, either at start or, with autoDeploy on, within a few seconds of the copy.

problem: "localhost is a name for the loopback address 127.0.0.1" is incomplete: on machines with IPv6 the hosts file usually also maps localhost to ::1, which is why a server bound only to 127.0.0.1 can refuse a localhost connection.
fix: localhost is a hostname that resolves to the loopback address, usually 127.0.0.1 (IPv4) and often also ::1 (IPv6), through the hosts file.

problem: "on the same machine address" is vague; students may read "machine" as the whole computer rather than one IP address.
fix: Why can Apache and IIS not both listen on the same IP address and port 80 on one machine?

problem: The step says to change Apache's Listen port but never states that the new port must then appear in every Apache URL, which is the mistake students actually make after the fix.
fix: After the change, Apache URLs must carry the new port, for example http://localhost:8080/shop/pay.php if Apache moves to 8080, and Tomcat must be moved off 8080 in server.xml.
